messages:
erica: Quick question — for new Private customers, are we leaning toward onboarding a lightweight relay agent (ephemeral tunnel + small sidecar) or just requiring a tenant NAT + private endpoint? Trying to weigh lifecycle and observability tradeoffs.

mike: My gut says relay for initial onboarding. Less infra friction for customers, we manage egress IPs and certs. But ops cost is higher.

sophia: Relay simplifies control-plane separation. We keep CP in our VPC and tunnel only dataplane. Telemetry + tracing works immediately.

erica: Right — downside is we need per-tenant process + upgrade surface. Any thoughts on autoscaling and resource isolation?

mike: Could be lightweight: single go binary with multiplexed tunnels, limit to 1000 rps per relay. Use ephemeral subconnections. If we pack many tenants per relay we must preserve tenant isolation at L7.

zoe: NAT approach reduces our runtime footprint in-customer but pushes complexity to customer network teams. Also harder to rotate CP certs without peering changes.

infra-bot: deploy-check: relay-proto v0.9 passes e2e connectivity tests in staging. 

sophia: Another angle — hybrid onboarding: start with relay for quick onboarding, then offer migration path to tenant NAT or VPC peering for long-lived customers. Provide a migration operator and playbook.

erica: That sounds pragmatic. Needs clear SLA differences documented and a migration runbook. I can draft an RFC follow-up that outlines: 1) relay lifetime & isolation model, 2) migration operator API, 3) telemetry guarantees, 4) failure modes and fallbacks (circuit-breaker to hosted fallback).

mike: +1. Add cost model (per-tenant relay-hours) and required contract language for Dedicated vs Private.

zoe: For the runbook, include sample iptables/netplan snippets and a minimal relay config example: ```relay:
  mode: multiplex
  max_conn: 200
  auth: mtls
```

sophia: And include rollout plan: alpha customers on relay, beta migration tooling, then GA with docs and CLI.

erica: Great — I'll open the RFC follow-up tomorrow and drop a short checklist here. Thanks everyone :pray:
